title: 'Wait for Time' with no time picked returns Success instantly — a silent no-op with no validation warning
what_happened: Added a Wait for Time node and left 'Wait Until' at its default empty state ('Select time...'). Pre-flight raised no issue for it. At runtime the log shows 'Executing child 3/3: Wait for Time' immediately followed by 'Child Wait for Time completed with status: Success' in the same millisecond (17:10:43.766494 -> 17:10:43.766505). No wait happened. Confirmed at source: rules/timing_rules.dart:17-18 does `if (waitUntil == null) continue;` so an unconfigured node produces no ValidationIssue at all.
expected: Either a preflight ERROR ('Wait for Time has no time set') or a runtime failure. The single most common use of this node is 'wait until astronomical dark before imaging'; silently skipping it starts the run in daylight.
repro: New sequence > add 'Wait for Time' > do not touch Wait Until > Start > Start Anyway. Node completes instantly.
proposed_fix: Emit a ValidationSeverity.error when WaitTimeNode.waitUntil == null (and when a Loop's repeatUntil is null under the RepeatUntil condition), and make the runtime fail rather than succeed.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Added a Wait for Time node, left Wait Until at 'Select time...' (node row honestly reads 'until (unset)'). Pre-flight (verify-43-pf2.png) listed only 'No Exposures' + a disk-space info — no issue for the unconfigured wait. Runtime, my app.log: 17:41:14.615986 '[PROGRESS_CB] Emitting NodeStarted: name=Wait for Time' -> 17:41:14.615998 'Child Wait for Time completed with status: Success'. 12 microseconds, no wait. Source confirms the named line: timing_rules.dart:17 `if (waitUntil == null) continue;`, and grep shows WaitTimeNode appears in exactly one file under providers/sequence/rules/, so no other rule covers it. Severity P1 stands — the canonical use is 'wait for astronomical dark', and skipping it starts the run in daylight.

title: Sequence header reports '0 frames / 0m' for a Science Photometry node that says '60 frames', and pre-flight claims 'No exposure nodes found'
what_happened: New sequence containing exactly one Science Photometry node. Its own row reads '(no target) · L · 60 frames' and its properties read Exposure 2.0 s, Frame count 60 (=2 min of integration). The toolbar planning chip reads '0 frames  0m'. Pre-flight adds a warning 'No Exposures — No exposure nodes found. The sequence will run but capture no images.' Earlier, a kitchen-sink sequence with 2 Science Photometry nodes plus 30 normal exposures also reported exactly '30 frames'. So the sequence-level frame count and time estimate ignore SciencePhotometryNode entirely.
expected: A photometry burst is the longest-running thing in a science sequence; the header must count its frames and its time, and the 'No Exposures' rule must not fire when a photometry node is present.
repro: New sequence > add 'Science Photometry' > read the toolbar chip vs the node row.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-47-photometry-frames.png (node row: '60 frames'; toolbar: '0 frames 0m'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-48-photprops.png (Exposure 2.0 s, Frame count 60)
proposed_fix: Include SciencePhotometryNode.count in the frame aggregate and its count x (exposure + download) in the duration aggregate; exclude it from the No-Exposures rule.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced for the frame count and the rule. A sequence containing exactly one Science Photometry node shows the node row '(no target) · Clear · 60 frames' while the toolbar chip reads '0 frames' (verify-16-photonly.png), and pre-flight raises 'No Exposures — No exposure nodes found. The sequence will run but capture no images.' (verify-18-photpreflight.png). Source: sequence_state.dart:170-178 `_countExposures` adds only ExposureNode and SmartExposureNode; exposure_rules.dart:150-156 NoExposuresRule tests only those two types. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) the duration half of the claim is wrong — SequenceTimeEstimator DOES account for SciencePhotometryNode (sequence_time_estimator.dart:618-627, count*exposure + download overhead + one filter change), so the proposed fix's duration clause is already implemented; the stale estimator is the separate `Sequence.estimateIntegrationSecs` walk (sequence_state.dart:315, ExposureNode only). (2) I never saw '0m' anywhere — this build's toolbar chip renders only a frame count. Severity down-called to P2: planning numbers lie, but the run itself captures correctly.

title: The Collapse button blanks the whole sequence tree to an empty grey rectangle
what_happened: With a 4-node sequence (1 target + Slew + Smart Exposure) I clicked 'Collapse' in the sequence header. The entire tree canvas rendered as a solid light-grey block with nothing drawn in it — no collapsed rows, no target card, nothing — while the header still read '1 target · 4 nodes' and the button flipped to 'Expand'. Clicking Expand restored the tree correctly. The sequence is completely unusable while collapsed.
expected: Collapse should show one collapsed row per top-level node.
repro: Build any sequence with a Target node > click 'Collapse' in the sequence header > wait 3s > screenshot.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. With [Science Photometry, Recovery, Target(New Target), Slew to Target] (header '1 target · 5 nodes'), clicking Collapse in the sequence header replaces the tree content below the first row with a solid light-grey block containing nothing — the Recovery row and the whole Target card vanish (verify-24-collapse2.png). The button flips to 'Expand', the header still reads '5 nodes / 1 target', and clicking Expand restores everything correctly (verify-45-postrun.png shows the tree intact afterwards). One correction: rows above the collapsed region (the Sequence header row and the first top-level instruction) still render, so 'the entire tree canvas' overstates it slightly — but the collapsed view is still unusable, which is the point. Note the button is inert on a sequence with no Target node (first attempt with 2 flat nodes did nothing at all), so a Target is required to repro.

title: The daylight gate blocks light frames only when a Target node is present — a targetless Take Exposures wrote 3 daylight LIGHT frames
what_happened: At 16:19 (Sun ~55 deg altitude) a sequence with no TargetHeader ran Take Exposures 3 x 2 s and wrote 3 IMAGETYP='Light' FITS files to disk with no gate at all. At 17:02, with the identical camera and sun position but the exposures under a TargetHeader, the runtime refused: 'Daylight gate: refusing light-frame exposure — Sun altitude 55.4 deg is above the maximum -12.0 deg for on-sky light imaging.' Slew is gated the same way. So forgetting to add a Target node silently removes the daylight protection for the exposures themselves.
expected: The daylight gate should key off frame type (light), not off whether a target group happens to exist.
repro: Sequence A: Take Exposures only (no Target) -> captures in daylight. Sequence B: Target > Smart Exposure -> refused by daylight gate.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced decisively, and with the variable isolated better than the original report (same node type on both sides, not Take Exposures vs Smart Exposure). Site set to lat 40 / lon -105, Sun ~63 deg. Sequence A = a bare 'Take Exposures' (LIGHT, 60s) with no TargetHeader: app.log 17:47:01.815050 'Starting 60.0s exposure', 17:48:02 'Saving FITS image to .../untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits', three frames written to disk, no gate anywhere in the log. Sequence B = the SAME Take Exposures node nested under a TargetHeader: app.log 17:53:17.075500 'Daylight gate: refusing light-frame exposure — Sun altitude 62.8 deg is above the maximum -12.0 deg for on-sky light imaging.' and the run failed. So the gate is keyed off the presence of a target group, not off frame type. Severity up-called from P2 to P1: this is a safety gate that a user disables by forgetting an unrelated node, and there is no warning that protection is off.

title: Every node failure is listed twice in the Session Report and raised as two identical toasts
what_happened: A single Open Cover node failed once; the Session Report Errors section listed 'Open Cover: No cover calibrator (flat panel) connected' twice and two identical Critical toasts appeared. Same with the single Start Guiding node ('Start Guiding: Failed to start guiding: No active guider configured' listed twice). The Open Dome run listed the same string 6 times because each internal retry was recorded as a separate error, so the report's error count never matches the number of failed nodes.
expected: One error entry per failed node (retries collapsed into 'failed after N attempts').
repro: Run a sequence containing exactly one Open Cover node with no cover calibrator connected; read the Session Report.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-34-cover-result.png (2 identical lines), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-46-final.png (2 identical lines), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-35-dome.png (6 identical lines)
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced three independent times on three different node types in my own session. (1) Open Dome: one failed node, Session Report Errors listed 'Open Dome: No dome connected' SEVEN times (verify-14-domefail.png) plus stacked Critical toasts. (2) Daylight gate: one failed exposure node, two identical 'Exposure: Daylight gate: refusing light-frame exposure...' lines and two identical Critical toasts (verify-66-state.png). (3) Run Script: one failed node, two identical 'Run Script: Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode' lines and two identical Critical toasts (verify-70-scriptdone.png). The error count therefore never matches the number of failed nodes, and retries inflate it further.

title: Pre-flight warns 'Slew to Target scheduled at 12:47 before target rises at 03:41'
what_happened: With a target at RA 6h30m Dec +40 (currently at altitude 89.3 deg, transiting in 6 minutes) pre-flight emitted two warnings: 'New Target: "Slew to Target" scheduled at 12:47 before target rises at 03:41' and the same for Smart Exposure at 12:48. 12:47 is nine hours AFTER 03:41, and the target is at the zenith. The comparison is clearly done on clock time without a date, so any target that rose earlier the same day is reported as not yet risen.
expected: Either no warning (the target is up) or a warning that names the correct night and the correct rise time.
repro: Add a Target with RA 6.5 h / Dec 40 at site lat 40, add Slew to Target, press Start around local noon.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim with the same coordinates. Site lat 40 / lon -105, target RA 6h30m00s Dec +40 00' 00". The target card itself computes Alt 77.8 deg, Airmass 1.02, Rise 03:41, Transit 12:48, Set 21:47 — i.e. the target is high in the sky right now. Pre-flight nonetheless warned: 'New Target: "Take Exposures" scheduled at 13:52 before target rises at 03:41' (verify-65-pf4.png). 13:52 is ten hours AFTER 03:41 on the same day, and the app's own altitude curve on the same screen contradicts the warning. The comparison is clock-time-only with no date, exactly as claimed.
